items.title: Mosquito fleets, hidden caves and drones: The battle for the Strait of Hormuz
items.description: By moving so much of the war into the Strait of Hormuz and Persian Gulf, Tehran has hit its adversaries where it hurts the most and analysts warn that while the United States military is mighty, history shows in asymmetrical warfare, the lesser power can win the day.

items.title: Live: Thousands more US Marines to be deployed to Middle East, officials say
items.description: The White House claims it could "take out" Iran's strategically important Kharg Island "any time" that Donald Trump gives the order.

items.title: What could happen to Australian fuel supplies after mid-April, according to experts
items.description: The government is responding to fuel shortages due to the war in the Middle East and says Australia has enough supply until mid-April. Here's what experts say could happen after that.

items.title: Chuck Norris, film star and martial artist, dies aged 86
items.description: Norris' epic fight with kung-fu superstar Bruce Lee in The Way of The Dragon helped him Norris into an icon, and he went on to star in more than 20 movies.

items.title: Fuel crisis a major political test for the Albanese government
items.description: Scott Morrison's assertion that the chase to secure vaccines in early 2021 was "not a race" cost him dearly. A similar global contest is already underway, only this time it involves securing energy supplies.

items.title: 'Not out of danger yet': Far North Queensland on flood alert as clean-up begins
items.description: Hundreds of millimetres of rain drench parts of Far North Queensland, with authorities urging residents to remain on flood watch as Tropical Cyclone Narelle recovery efforts begin.

items.title: Iran war 'worst' time for tax, say gas companies
items.description: The Greens and One Nation are among those that want gas profits levied, with pressure mounting on Labor to respond to growing calls for reform.

items.title: Woman's death at remote hospital deemed preventable by coroner
items.description: The coroner found that a mother of three could have been saved if a transfer from a remote New South Wales hospital had been ordered sooner.

items.title: Alice Springs prison guards go on 12-hour strike over 'unsafe' conditions
items.description: Alice Springs prison guards have taken industrial action, including a 12-hour work stoppage across the town's correctional facilities, over what they say are unsafe conditions.

items.title: Norway's Crown Princess says she was 'deceived' by Epstein
items.description: Norway's Crown Princess has told national TV that she had been "manipulated and deceived" by Jeffrey Epstein and wished she had never met him.

items.title: Fashion industry pins survival strategy on new Australian-made push
items.description: Australia's peak clothing and textile organisation launches a national strategy to revitalise an industry hit by years of turmoil.

items.title: Giddey sets new Aussie NBA record as Bulls fall short of miracle comeback
items.description: Josh Giddey continues his remarkable form but it is not enough to give the Chicago Bulls a much-needed win.

items.title: Australian Olympic champ McEvoy breaks 17yo world record
items.description: Australia's Cameron McEvoy sets a world record in the men's 50 metres freestyle, dipping under the previous mark that had stood since 2009.

items.title: Brisbane pull off grand final repeat in rematch with Storm
items.description: The stakes might not have been as high as last year's grand final but Brisbane followed the same script with a rollicking comeback win over Melbourne in the rematch of last year's decider.

items.title: Bulldog Baker's brilliant goal seals thrilling win over fast-finishing Crows
items.description: The Western Bulldogs hang on to claim a thrilling six-point win over Adelaide, with a brilliant Oskar Baker goal clinching the win as the Crows stormed home.

items.title: Greig Fraser filmed the unfilmable for Dune. Now he's back for Project Hail Mary
items.description: With most of Project Hail Mary's action taking place in far off corners of space it was up to Australian cinematographer Greig Fraser to create what we've never seen.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of 2000s hip-hop, Mercury in retrograde and disturbing TV puppets
items.description: Every question has only two options: one is right and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: Finding an escape from modern life in the booming world of arts and crafts
items.description: Craft trends come and go, but a resurgence in social arts and crafts is proving that creativity and human connection are still very much in vogue.

items.title: Donor devastated as charity plans to sell land despite agreement not to
items.description: A charity known for the landmark separation of conjoined twins Krishna and Trishna lists a regional Victorian property for sale against the wishes of its donor.

items.title: One Nation candidate wanted in UK on sexual touching charge
items.description: South Australian One Nation candidate Aoi Baxter has a warrant for his arrest in the UK after he failed to show up to court to face a charge of sexually touching a woman without consent.

items.title: 'Asking why honey is better than s***': Japan coach spins favouritism ahead of Matildas clash
items.description: Japan's coach says determining a favourite for the Women's Asian Cup final between his team and Australia is a matter for bees and flies.

items.title: While the US is busy in Iran, China is pushing on with its geopolitical agenda
items.description: Donald Trump has postponed a meeting with Xi Jinping because he is busy with Iran and the Middle East — and that's good news for China.

items.title: Trump jokes about Pearl Harbor in front of visibly uncomfortable Japanese PM
items.description: When he was asked why the US did not notify allies like Japan ahead of the strikes on Iran, Donald Trump made a quip drawing a parallel with the Japanese air raid in 1941.

items.title: Banksy's anonymity has been shredded along with the mystery of his work
items.description: Does Banksy's success mean we are more entitled to demand he pull his mask off, show his face? Does it matter that he says his anonymity is core to his art?

items.title: Epworth releases details of hospital review after surgeon allegations
items.description: A South Australian health commissioner will lead the review of clinical governance at Epworth Hospital, after allegations a top gynaecologist performed unnecessary operations to remove endometriosis.
